This page lists every Excel function used in the course with its
French-language equivalent. Functions are grouped by the module where
they are first introduced.

> **Note on locales**: If your Excel uses a French locale, function names
> and list separators differ (e.g., `AVERAGE` → `MOYENNE`; `,` → `;`).
> The formulas in this course use **English function names** and comma
> separators. Use the table below to translate.

## Module 1 — First steps

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SUM` | `SOMME` | Add a range of numbers |
| `COUNT` | `NB` | Count numeric cells |
| `COUNTA` | `NBVAL` | Count non-empty cells |
| `IF` | `SI` | Conditional logic |
| `AND` | `ET` | Logical AND |
| `OR` | `OU` | Logical OR |
| `MIN` | `MIN` | Smallest value |
| `MAX` | `MAX` | Largest value |
| `LARGE` | `GRANDE.VALEUR` | k-th largest value |
| `TODAY` | `AUJOURDHUI` | Current date |
| `MONTH` | `MOIS` | Month number from a date |

## Module 2 — Frequency tables & charts

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `COUNTIF` | `NB.SI` | Count cells matching one criterion |
| `COUNTIFS` | `NB.SI.ENS` | Count cells matching multiple criteria |
| `SUMIF` | `SOMME.SI` | Sum cells matching one criterion |

## Module 3 — Histograms & cumulative curves

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `COUNTIFS` | `NB.SI.ENS` | Class counts with range criteria (`>=lower`, `<upper`) |
| *PivotTable grouping* | *Regroupement TCD* | Right-click a numeric field → **Group** to bin automatically |

## Module 4 — Central tendency

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AVERAGE` | `MOYENNE` | Arithmetic mean |
| `MEDIAN` | `MEDIANE` | Median (50th percentile) |
| `MODE.SNGL` | `MODE.SIMPLE` | Single most frequent value |
| `SUMPRODUCT` | `SOMMEPROD` | Weighted mean (`=SUMPRODUCT(values, weights)/SUM(weights)`) |

## Module 5 — Position & boxplot

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `QUARTILE.EXC` | `QUARTILE.EXCLURE` | Exclusive quartiles (position `(n+1)*q`) — **course standard** |
| `PERCENTILE.EXC` | `CENTILE.EXCLURE` | Exclusive percentiles — **course standard** |
| `MIN` | `MIN` | Minimum (for five-number summary) |
| `MAX` | `MAX` | Maximum (for five-number summary) |
| *Box & Whisker chart* | *Graphique Boîte à moustaches* | Insert → Charts → Statistical → Box and Whisker |

> **Why `QUARTILE.EXC`?** The course follows the `(n+1)*q` position formula
> (OpenStax §2.2), which matches Excel's exclusive method. `QUARTILE.INC`
> (inclusive) gives different values on small samples — do not mix them.

## Module 6 — Dispersion

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `VAR.S` | `VAR.S` | Sample variance (denominator `n-1`) — **course standard** |
| `STDEV.S` | `ECARTYPE.STANDARD` | Sample standard deviation — **course standard** |
| `VAR.P` | `VAR.P.N` | Population variance (denominator `n`) |
| `STDEV.P` | `ECARTYPE.PEARSON` | Population standard deviation |
| `SUMSQ` | `SOMME.CARRES` | Sum of squares (for variance shortcut) |
| `FILTER` | `FILTRE` | Keep only the rows of `tblFork` that match a condition (e.g. one franchise) inside another function |

> **Sample vs population**: This is a descriptive statistics course.
> We use the **sample** formulas (`.S`) by default because real business
> data are almost always samples. The population variants (`.P`) are
> shown for completeness.

## Module 7 — Shape

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SKEW` | `COEFFICIENT.ASYMETRIE` | Adjusted Fisher–Pearson skewness (sample) |

> **Kurtosis**: No Excel function is used — kurtosis is treated
> conceptually only (names and pictures).

## Module 8 — Bivariate I

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `COUNTIFS` | `NB.SI.ENS` | Two-way contingency table counts |
| *PivotTable (two fields)* | *TCD (deux champs)* | Rows = one variable, Columns = another, Values = Count |
| *XY Scatter chart* | *Nuage de points* | Insert → Charts → Scatter |

## Module 9 — Bivariate II

| English | Français | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `COVARIANCE.S` | `COVARIANCE.STANDARD` | Sample covariance |
| `COVARIANCE.P` | `COVARIANCE.PEARSON` | Population covariance |
| `CORREL` | `COEFFICIENT.CORRELATION` | Pearson correlation coefficient *r* |
| `SLOPE` | `PENTE` | Least-squares slope *b* |
| `INTERCEPT` | `ORDONNEE.ORIGINE` | Least-squares intercept *a* |
| `RSQ` | `COEFFICIENT.DETERMINATION` | Coefficient of determination *R²* |
| *Data Analysis → Regression* | *Données → Analyse → Régression* | Full regression output table (Analysis ToolPak) |

## Module 10 — Synthesis

All functions from Modules 1–9.

## French locale tips

- **List separator**: French Excel uses `;` instead of `,` between arguments.
  - English: `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` → French: `=MOYENNE(A1:A10)` (same here)
  - English: `=IF(A1>0, "pos", "neg")` → French: `=SI(A1>0; "pos"; "neg")`
- **Decimal separator**: French uses `,` (comma) for decimals; English uses `.` (point).
  - The CSV files in this course use `.` as decimal separator.
- **Function names**: The table above gives the exact French names. If a
  function is not listed, it may not have a localised name (rare).

## Unverified French names

The following French names are inferred from Microsoft documentation
and have not been tested in a live French Excel. Please verify before
relying on them in an exam setting:

- `QUARTILE.EXC` → `QUARTILE.EXCLURE`
- `PERCENTILE.EXC` → `CENTILE.EXCLURE`
- `VAR.S` → `VAR.S` (may be `VAR.S` in both locales)
- `STDEV.S` → `ECARTYPE.STANDARD`
- `COVARIANCE.S` → `COVARIANCE.STANDARD`
- `COVARIANCE.P` → `COVARIANCE.PEARSON`
- `SKEW` → `COEFFICIENT.ASYMETRIE`
- `RSQ` → `COEFFICIENT.DETERMINATION`
